page: Microsoft Azure HB368-240rs_v5 is a high-performance computing instance within the HBv5 series, engineered for tightly coupled computational tasks. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor and managed through Microsoft Hyper-V, the platform allocates 240 dedicated vCPUs alongside 448.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes a memory density of 1.87 GB per core, tailoring the system to compute-dense algorithms where multi-threaded throughput takes precedence over extensive per-core RAM capacity.

Storage and network architectures are provisioned to support intensive data transfers. The instance features 15875 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, facilitating rapid read and write access for large scratch files without incurring network storage latency. Complementing local storage, the instance supports Premium Storage and incorporates RDMA networking capabilities to enable low-latency communication across distributed nodes. The server contains no discrete GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Qualitatively, the server achieves efficiency in high-scale environments by pairing high compute density with massive local NVMe capacity, minimizing the cost overhead of attached external disks for temporary dataset processing. A key architectural tradeoff is the restricted per-core memory footprint, which necessitates partitioning or algorithmic optimizations for memory-heavy datasets. The HB368-240rs_v5 is suited for MPI-based parallel clusters, computational fluid dynamics, engineering simulations, and large batch-processing workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure HB368-240rs_v5 is a dedicated high-performance computing virtual machine within the HBv5 series, provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system features 240 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel processor, matched with 448.0 GB of system memory to deliver 1.87 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture includes 15875 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity alongside Premium Storage capabilities, supporting data-intensive scratch operations. High-speed interconnectivity is facilitated by RDMA support for multi-node clustering, while the instance excludes discrete GPU accelerators and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The dense compute profile and substantial local NVMe volume provide strong qualitative cost efficiency for execution pipelines that process high-throughput data locally without requiring massive memory allocations per core. Consequently, HB368-240rs_v5 fits high-performance computing simulations, computational fluid dynamics, large-scale distributed batch processing, and high-throughput analytical workloads.
